headline: McKinsey Analyst | MIT 2025
about: I am a passionate technologist aspiring to help solve the world's most challenging problems and eliminate ambiguity and uncertainty. My hope is to find people who are just as hungry and passionate as I am, and who are just as committed to helping make the world feel closer and more familiar than before. I've had a lifelong love of technology in all its forms. I first learned I loved computer science in 5th grade when I programmed a game in scratch.mit.edu and showed it to my friends. I am proud to have graduated from MIT in 2025 with a degree in AI and Decision-Making. While I was there, I dabbled in some research and worked in startups and the big tech world as a software engineer. More recently, I've been getting more involved in the business side of technology at McKinsey & Company. I believe that place is the best place for me to learn the management and communication skills I need to lead large teams and drive big change. I have some big ambitions for the technology industry. One day, I hope to have some part in reshaping the very culture of that industry for the better. If something like that interests you, feel free to message me! I would love to chat.

headline: McKinsey Business Analyst | ND '24
about: I am from Monterrey, Mexico, and am also a U.S. citizen. I recently graduated from the University of Notre Dame after studying Computer Science as my Major, as well as a Minor in Engineering Corporate Practice. I've always been incredibly interested in the intersection between technology and business, and have grown to be very passionate about consulting, finding innovative approaches to solve different issues, and thinking about newfound technologies and the way they impact the world around us daily.

profileTopEducation.schoolName: University of Notre Dame

experience.companyName: ALPFA, Inc - Association of Latino Professionals For America
experience.description: ALPFA's mission is to empower and develop Latino men and women as leaders of character for the nation, in every sector of the global economy. I acted as the liaison between Accenture & ALPFA at the University of Notre Dame, directing and planning Accenture’s on-campus recruiting events. Also, we members of the board were constantly working to provide improved support, outlets, and recruiting connections to other fellow Latinos on campus.

I worked as an ambassador for PredictionStrike, with the main goal of spreading the word and increasing the application's presence on campuses across the United States. PredictionStrike is a venture-backed sports investing startup that is on the rise, and it was an incredible experience to play a part in that growth and do my best to help it spread as much as possible.

I was selected to attend an in-person two-day conference that brings together some of the most incredible, gifted, and passionate college students across the United States. This event at Salesforce's Chicago office was an opportunity to learn more about their various non-technical intern and new graduate roles, and essentially to explore the possibilities of launching a business career in the tech industry. I also had the opportunity to participate in workshops and networking sessions while learning a lot, so I am incredibly grateful to have been a part of this wonderful experience!

experience.location: New York, New York, United States
experience.description: I had the amazing opportunity to be a part of EY's Launch internship program, specifically working as a Technology Rotation Consulting Intern. I worked on two different projects. The first one was in FSO Technology Consulting, which allowed me to develop the environment strategy for the next stage of the sprint project development to address the client’s desires, and I also got to assist with updating the budgeting of the team and project to meet goals and stay within a specific profit margin. In the second project, I created a program dashboard on Mural delineating project divisions, tasks, and content to present to the clients. Overall, this experience was truly incredible, and I am very grateful for the growth, skills, and lessons I received as a result.

I had the amazing opportunity to attend an online two-day conference that brings together some of the best, brightest, and most diverse college students across North America. I had the opportunity to explore career possibilities at Cognizant, participate in learning activities, and network with peers and Cognizant professionals. Built into this amazing two-day event was also an interactive learning experience through Forage, in which I got to learn more about the Agile model as well as artificial intelligence at Cognizant.

I had the amazing opportunity to be a participant in Goldman Sachs' 2022 Engineering Possibilities Summit. Throughout the summit, I was able to sharpen my technical skills through activities and interactive workshops, while also building connections with Goldman Sachs professionals and program participants. Additionally, I connected with several divisions to find the role that best leveraged my
strengths, and learned an incredible amount from all of the amazing people I met.

I had the opportunity to be a part of two different travel teams during my freshman year. The first project was with Microsoft, in which we worked on improving the existing Microsoft Learn platform to make it more accessible, effective, and efficient for all types of users. The second project was with Amazon, specifically targeting how to improve Amazon Fresh sales due to the COVID-19 pandemic, for which we devised a three-pronged approach including a revamped website with a new college program. Afterwards, in my sophomore year, I was given the opportunity to be the project leader for the Nayaraq & Accenture Social Impact Project. For this project, my team and I analyzed different revenue generation models to help Nayaraq evolve into a financially sustainable organization that can address gender equity in Latin America more effectively.

I worked as an intern at METAK, which is a company that manufactures & repairs hydraulic cylinders. This was an incredibly valuable experience because I gained lots of insight into different Engineering disciplines and fields, as I got to assist workers with all sorts of machinery and different tasks at stations. I also helped organize the storage and keep track of materials, or sometimes even checking the concentration of chrome for the hard chrome plating and the concentration of sulfate in the chromic acid bath.

projects.description: This is a 3-hour individual lecture given at University of Hong Kong with systematic presentation on term-structure models of interest rates, mainly following the pedagogical approaches in Duffie (1996).

projects.title: Facial Keypoints Detection
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Stanford University
projects.description: In this project, we are given a list of 96×96-pixel 8-bit graylevel images with their corresponding (x,y) coordinates of 15 facial keypoints. We first adopt hold-out cross validation to randomly split the data set into a training set and a test set, so that we can develop our algorithm on the training set and assess its performance on the test set. Our algorithm first performs histogram stretching to enhance the image contrast by stretching the range of pixel intensity of each training image. Then, in order for noise reduction, we apply principal components analysis on the stretched images to obtain the eigenfaces. Using the resultant eigenfaces, we implement the mean patch searching algorithm with correlation scoring and mutual information scoring to predict the left- and right-eye centers for any query test facial images.

projects.title: Predicting Unemployment in the Great Recession
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Stanford University
projects.description: Based on survey information spanning from 1979 to 2006 on over 3,900 observations, this project predicts the number of weeks that each query person was unemployed during 2010, at the peak of the Great Recession. To improve the prediction accuracy, we perform missing data imputation techniques, apply Lasso regression (with cross validation) to select the significant predictors, and then utilize random forest method to produce predictions.

projects.title: Exact Closed Form Formulas and Saddlepoint Approximation Methods for Pricing VIX Derivatives under Alternative Stochastic Volatility Models
projects.associatedWith: Associated with The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
projects.description: Volatility derivatives, as a special class of financial derivatives whose underlying asset is the volatility, have witnessed increasing popularity over the last decades. Among assorted measurements of volatility, the Volatility Index (VIX) launched by the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) is most closely followed by investors, and its derivatives, namely, the VIX futures and options, are the most actively traded products. Therefore, a solid understanding of the VIX index as well as accurate and efficient pricing of the VIX futures and options are called for. This thesis serves as a self-contained monograph on this topic. A systematic and comprehensive introduction to the VIX index is first presented. Then, the exact closed form pricing formulas for the VIX futures and options are derived under the stochastic volatility model with simultaneous jumps and the 3/2 plus jumps stochastic volatility model, respectively. Furthermore, the saddlepoint approximation pricing formulas of different orders are proposed for the VIX futures and options under the stochastic volatility model with simultaneous jumps, which are brand-new in the area of VIX derivatives pricing. Finally, results from numerical tests are reported.

projects.title: Approximation to a Class of Financial Derivatives
projects.associatedWith: Associated with City University of Hong Kong
projects.description: This independent project first approximates option price under the Black-Scholes model by the PDE method and the equivalent martingale method, both leading to the celebrated Black-Scholes formula. Then it extends to solving more general models such as constant elasticity of variance (CEV) model by numerical methods with appropriate boundary conditions, in which financial bubbles may nonetheless occur.

experience.description:
As a consultant, I worked primarily in project management and functional roles in large Workday Finance, Human Capital Management, and Payroll Implementations. Highlights include:

-Redesigned and implemented a more efficient payroll accounting process to pay 15,000 public employees across 37 different institutions on a Workday HCM and finance implementation at one of the largest public university systems in the country.

- Advised and led the audit of a Workday implementation spanning across the finance, HR, payroll, and supply chain functions at a large university, providing mitigation strategies to overcome project risks.

- Managed and coordinated a team of 9 senior experts to analyze project metrics and qualitative data taken from interviews with client stakeholders and identify areas of concern

Alcoa Inc. is one of the largest lightweight metal manufacturing companies in the world. Alcoa's Tennessee Operations is principally responsible for producing the sheet metal used to make beverage cans for companies such as Coca-Cola and Anheuser Busch, and automotive parts for Ford among other car manufacturers. 

In my role, I had the opportunity to learn about and participate in some of the financial processes required to support such a large manufacturing operation. My main goal this summer was to improve the processes the finance group at Alcoa-TN Operations uses to collect, record and analyze data. In order to improve these processes I first had to gain an intimate understanding of them, so in my two month internship, I was able to learn a lot about how financial analysis works. 

Almost all of the production and revenue data at TN-Ops is tracked through excel spreadsheets. My projects consisted of redesigning and updating these spreadsheets to fit the needs of the user. These spreadsheets had to take the entered data and calculate the relevant outputs while being easy to use and fitting the needs of the user. The end result of my internship is that now many of the financial analysts' activities can be completed more efficiently. 

I also worked with internal controls. I designed a flowchart to be used during corporate audits and participated in a physical inventory. 

In my role as a finance intern, I participated in financial processes like closing, forecasting, and bridging at a major corporation. In my role, I used SAP, Oracle and Excel to gather and analyze data. I honed my Excel and spreadsheet design skills, so now, I am very confident in my ability with this tool. I learned a lot about accounting and financial analysis at a large corporation and had the opportunity to make a lasting impact on the way members of the finance group complete their tasks.

I naturally gravitate towards work experiences that foster a collaborative, fast-paced, and meritocratic team environment, where each member uplifts and supports one another. projects.title: Experimental modal analysis of a metal plate using different excitation methods
projects.associatedWith: Associated with University of Cincinnati
projects.description:
This project deals with the modal analysis of a simple rectangular and a circular plate. The modal analysis was carried out using XModal software.

1. Different excitation techniques (Impact hammer, sine sweep, chirp and various types of random excitation) were used and their appropriate windows were employed. For all the cases, the coherence at the FRF peaks were checked. 

2. Mode indicator functions were used to detect repeated roots and MVCP was used to check the normality of the mode.

3. First 28 modes were extracted successfully from the generated data.

projects.title: Generation of RPM and Order spectral maps using MATLAB
projects.associatedWith: Associated with University of Cincinnati
projects.description:
This project dealt with the generation of RPM and Order spectral maps from the raw tachometer and sensor data taken from a rotating machine.

1. Various ways to generate an accurate instantaneous speed (Hilbert transforms, TVDFT, COT, and adaptive algorithms) curve were studied and generated using MATLAB.

2. With the help of the instantaneous speed curve, the RPM and order spectral maps were generated using MATLAB.

projects.title: Evaluation of FRF from a MIMO time data using MATLAB
projects.associatedWith: Associated with University of Cincinnati
projects.description:
This project deals with the evaluation of the Frequency Response Function (FRF) – log magnitude and phase, multiple coherence and virtual forces for the given Multi Input Multi Output data (MIMO) (3 input and 4 output channels) using MATLAB

1. Main aim was to observe the changes in noise and leakage in the FRF data due to usage of techniques like cyclic averaging and overlap processing and the effects of using different types of windows, averages and block sizes. 

2. H1 and HV algorithms were used for FRF calculation and the benefits of using HV were observed. 

3. 3 types of windows (Hanning, flat top and rectangular), 4 types of averages (linear, power spectrum, magnitude and PSD) and 2 different block sizes were used for comparison in conjunction with overlap processing and cyclic averaging.

projects.title: FEA analysis of a rotor-stator system with flexible bearings using ANSYS Workbench
projects.associatedWith: Associated with University of Cincinnati
projects.description:
A simple shaft-rotor system was modeled in ANSYS workbench for the project.
1. Initially, the natural frequency of the system is obtained and the results validated mathematically, using Transfer Matrix method.

2. The effect of changing the stiffness of the bearings on the natural frequency of the system was observed.

3.  Campbell diagrams were plotted for both the cases, to understand the effect of gyroscopic stiffening on natural frequencies of the system. 

4. Further, the effect of unbalance mass on the system was observed by adding an unbalance mass and plotting the FRF for a point on the system.

projects.title: Rider comfort evaluation of a motorbike – On road evaluation
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Bajaj Auto Ltd
projects.description:
This project dealt with the evaluation of peak and average vibration levels felt at the human interface points (HIPs) in a motorbike.
1. Headed the measurement and instrumentation side of the project. Actively coordinated with the design team for suggestions and improvements to existing design in comparison with benchmark vehicles.

2. The exercise was carried out for a set of practical on-road conditions including potholes, speed bumps etc.

projects.title: Modal correlation of a frame-engine assembly in a motorbike
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Bajaj Auto Ltd
projects.description:
This project dealt with the complete modal analysis and correlation of those results using CAE software for a complete frame-engine assembly of a motorbike.

• A bottom up approach was adopted for the project, i.e. starting from correlation of sub components leading up to the correlation of the assembly.

• The model was created using Altair hyperworks and was correlated with the Modal analysis performed using B&K software. Various errors in modeling and the testing were rectified and process standardized to achieve a high correlation.

• MAC values and mode shapes obtained from Me’Scope software were used as the comparison criteria.

projects.title: Mathematical Modeling of an engine mount system
projects.associatedWith: Associated with National Institute of Technology Tiruchirappalli
projects.description:
This work reports on the mathematical modeling of an Engine Mount system to determine modal characteristics.

• For the modeling, a car containing a 3 cylinder inline engine was considered. The mathematical model was created using MATLAB with a passive mount first and then a semi active mount. 

• The second phase involves comparing the responses with semi active mount in place of a passive mount. As it is the ride comfort that matters the most, the comparison of forces transmitted to chassis for both types of mounts, using the mathematical model, are performed. The design parameters for the semi active mount are then tuned to give favorable responses over a wide range of Engine RPM.

projects.title: Failure Analysis of the Super Heater Coils of a FBC boiler
projects.associatedWith: Associated with National Institute of Technology Tiruchirappalli
projects.description:
This project dealt with modelling and analysis of the Super Heater Coils of a FBC boiler for BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited).
• The existing model was failing under the operating conditions and a new model had to be proposed with minimal changes to the existing model.
• Thermal, Pressure and contact loads were used in the analysis and a new model with optimized location of support brackets was suggested and implemented.

headline: Partner (in Manufacturing & Supply Chain) at McKinsey and Company;    Global co-lead, Supply Chain Planning Practice;  Head, SCM Connections; Head, NA Operations Excellence Program
about:
A Partner in McKinsey’s Chicago office, I am a leader in the North America Operations - Manufacturing and Supply Chain - practice. I am the global co-lead of McKinsey's Supply Chain Planning (PLAN) service line.  I sponsored the acquisition of SCM Connections and am leading the integration and responsible for the asset.  I also lead our technology vendor alliances in Planning.  I also founded and grew our DELIVER service line that covers warehousing, transportation and network optimization.

Since joining the Firm in 2003, I have focused on broad operations and supply chain efforts with my clients across industries including projects on Supply Chain design, diagnostics, transformation, digital transformations using advanced analytics and AI/ML, inventory reduction, operations strategy, lean transformations (plants/warehouses), transportation optimization, SKU optimization/ complexity reduction and network optimization.  

Prior to joining McKinsey, I was the Managing Director (CEO) of Megha Insulations Pvt. Ltd. (a Calcium Silicate Insulation manufacturer in India), where I led turnaround of the company from near bankruptcy. I was responsible for setting up greenfield project including the arrangement of term loans and working capital finance, sourcing and erection of plant and equipment. I was solely responsible for day to day operations and setting up sourcing, supply and distribution.

Outside of the office, I have also been a guest lecturer for Supply Chain at Kellogg School of Management and have delivered keynote addresses and webinars in various forums - e.g. HBR, DHL Lifesciences conference, Logipharma, Logimed, Kinaxis, SAP partner events

As an archival assistant intern at the Lewistown Public Library, I am increasing the general public's easy access to documents with local historical significance by developing an online free archival repository. publications.title: Distorsiones Cambiarias y Flujo de Remesas en Venezuela para el Período 1997-2014
publications.description:
Estudio acerca de cómo las distorsiones cambiarias, representadas por la prima de mercado negro, afectaron el flujo de remesas por canales formales en Venezuela, motivando a la sobre-utilización de mecanismos formales de envío hacia el extranjero y a la sub-utilización de mecanismos formales de recepción desde el resto del mundo. publications.title: El papel de la dimensión colectiva en el estudio de la felicidad.
publications.description: Los estudios sobre felicidad incluyen diversas perspectivas, conceptualizaciones y factores asociados a este concepto; sin embargo, las investigaciones sobre felicidad con frecuencia se concentran en la dimensión individual de la misma. El presente trabajo hace énfasis en la concepción de la felicidad como un constructo multidimensional conformado por aspectos individuales y por aspectos colectivos. De manera que el propósito central del artículo es presentar un análisis sobre la dimensión colectiva de la felicidad, la cual ha sido poco estudiada en el contexto latinoamericano. En particular este artículo busca enfatizar el papel de las relaciones afectivas, la conducta prosocial y la inversión en los demás, en la comprensión de la felicidad. En las conclusiones se identifican temáticas relevantes asociadas a la dimensión colectiva que permitirán ampliar la investigación sobre la felicidad.

projects.title: The FlexiWash
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Northwestern University
projects.description:
Our project sought to resolve a problem given to us by Ms. Isabel Márquez from the Rehabilitation Institute of Chicago. She stated that her patients who have limited mobility in one side of their body have trouble washing the dishes, and our task was to facilitate this action by designing a physical product. This project aims to help patients at the RIC more easily wash the dishes and become more independent.
 
Our design, dubbed the Flexi-Wash, is meant to stabilize plates, bowls, and cups in the sink so that people with limited mobility in one vertical side of their bodies may more easily wash the dishes. The FlexiWash is a multi-tiered box that is flat on the top of each tier to hold plates, and angled closer to the center of each tier to accommodate bowls. The FlexiWash would ideally be coated entirely with a non-slip material called dycem (which will reduce plate slippage).The FlexiWash also has drainage holes placed in each corner of the second and third levels as well as one large drain hole in the center so as to allow water to escape.
In order to accommodate cups and silverware, the FlexiWash was designed for compatibility with the FlexiWash accessories, namely the scrubbing strip and cup-washing accessory. The scrubbing strip is located on the side of the FlexiWash and is a steel wool strip attached by hooks, and the cup-washing accessory is a dycem cup-holder that fits snugly into the center of the FlexiWash. Overall, the FlexiWash is a simple, effective, and safe solution to the problem of washing tableware with one hand.

experience.companyName: A Body in a Station by Eiko Otake
experience.description:
Eiko Otake is a movement-based, interdisciplinary artist that received a MacArthur Fellowship in 1996 as part of Eiko & Koma. 

A Body in a Station bears witness to human transformation. People traversing the space are literally and figuratively in transition from one state to another—from home to work, from high school to college, from loneliness to an encounter and sometimes the reverse. Many are rushing to and fro; many are waiting. Some have no other place to go. In the construct of a performance where viewers are not in darkness, rather walking by or gathering around the performer, observers are themselves being observed, by each other and by the lone Eiko.

Part of Lower Manhattan Cultural Council's River to River Festival.

Review featured in New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/25/arts/dance/eiko-otake-holds-a-mourning-service-at-rush-hour.html?_r=1

projects.title: Engineering Senior Capstone: Optimizing Course Scheduling for Olin Business School
projects.description: The process of course scheduling in the Olin Business School at Washington University in St. Louis is incredibly labor and time intensive. Olin’s Assistant Dean, completes it by hand, taking her approximately a month to find a feasible schedule for over 350 classes. We streamline this process by developing an integer program that finds feasible and optimal schedules using data from the Spring 2019 semester. Our program will drastically save time for Olin administrators, who will be able to use it as a scheduling tool for future semesters. The formulation is written using Python, solved using the optimization tool Gurobi Solver, and exported to Excel using XLWT for easy visualization and comprehension. We succeed in not only finding a feasible schedule, but also finding an optimal schedule. We experiment with different objective functions by incorporating professor, administrative, and student preferences, allowing us to present multiple schedules to the Olin administration.

headline: Partner at McKinsey & Company
about:
Teresa George is a Partner at McKinsey & Company where she partners with companies across sectors to transform financial and operational performance.  Her expertise and experience are in supply chain and procurement, however, over the course of most transformations she advises clients on broader operations and organizational change. Teresa works across sectors, with extensive experience in travel, hospitality, advanced industries, banking, and financial services. 

In service to her local community, Teresa co-leads McKinsey & Company’s Chicago Community Consulting (CCC).  CCC is a group of consultants who volunteer on pro bono engagements to help Chicago-based non-profits and cultural institutions define strategy, drive growth and improve operations. 

Outside of McKinsey, Teresa serves on the Executive Board of Girls on the Run-Chicago and Board of Trustees for the Chicago Academy of Sciences / Peggy Notebaert Nature Museum.  Teresa is deeply passionate about Chicago and non-profit work in the local community.  It brings her great joy and fulfillment. 

Before joining McKinsey in 2012, Teresa was a managing consultant at IBM Global Business Services where her love for consulting including helping individuals and organizations solve the toughest challenges blossomed.  Teresa has a B.S. in Business Administration from The Ohio State University.  

Teresa's personal interests including spending time with her family and friends, traveling the world, cooking, reading, and yoga.

I am a strategist, trusted advisor, and authentic thought leader dedicated to advancing social and public sector issues that make life-changing impacts on individuals, neighborhoods, and cities.

I hold core beliefs and aspirations that guide and shape every endeavor I engage in:
* Everyone deserves a first-rate education.
* Innovative ideas brought to scale transform people and their communities.

My passion for providing equitable opportunities for all people has driven me to engage, influence, and partner with school system leaders, nonprofit executives, foundation boards, and individual donors in developing, funding, and implementing transformative initiatives.

As a trusted advisor to school districts, national foundations, and other major institutions, I managed 30+ high-impact engagements with K-12 and higher education systems, leading philanthropies, and private sector organizations.

receivedRecommendations.description:
Doug is one of the most thoughtful leaders I have worked with. He is incredibly sharp, capable, empathetic, and reliably even keeled even during times of chaos and our virtual COVID work environment. Doug is a quick learner and defines team player. No problem or task is too large or too small for Doug to get involved. He not only leads the strategic, thought-provoking discussions, but is also willing to roll up his sleeves and put his ideas on paper to solicit feedback. When he joined the Corporate Coalition, the idea of launching a Resiliency Network was all theoretical. Doug took this concept - led a team of experts to design it, defined the program and how companies would get involved, then sold it to 10 companies, and now is overseeing the execution of the first cohort and its curriculum in action - all within 9 months!

Doug talks the talk and walks the walk. After he understands the task ahead, he brings order to chaos while still allowing for levity and protecting his people by making sure colleagues are not working long hours on superfluous tasks.  He is always looking for feedback, ways to improve, and how to engage everyone in conversation. Doug innately lifts everyone around him up - he is a great listener and champion of others. When onboarding a new team member - he asks, "How can we make sure he/she is having fun?" When I needed help pitching my ideas and concepts to our extended team and Managing Director, Doug made time to review my presentation, help me think through the strategy and reassure me so that I was ready to clearly communicate my ideas, facilitate a discussion and field questions with confidence.

Simply put, Doug is a bright, reliable and insightful team player and leader. We continue to benefit tremendously from Doug's leadership and I know he would be an asset for any organization that is fortunate enough to work with him!

What impressed me so deeply about his analysis was not just his ability to cut to the core of complex issues, but even more was the efficiency with which he did so. Prashob always seemed to be able to identify key data points for the analysis, take a question to it's logical conclusion, and (most impressively) know just when to stop on a particular line of inquiry. 

Beyond his consulting work, Prashob proved to be an excellent manager and mentor during my time at Accenture. He consistently advocated for me, aligned opportunities that were consistent with my skill set, and then mentored me through the work. I am certain that as his career progresses Prashob will prove to be a highly effective leader of increasingly larger teams. 

Finally, beyond the office, I was impressed with Prashob's personal drive and self discipline. It may seem a small detail but Prashob was the only member of the team who made it a point to hit the gym every night. Given there were days when we left work after 8, this meant Prashob was willing to put off eating dinner till 9 or 10 in order to be consistent with his personal routine. This level of dedication, consistency, and drive is a hallmark of Prashob's character, and is certainly indicative of the work he did for our client. 

Therefore given Prashob's extraordinary analytical skills, managerial talent, and personal self discipline, it is my pleasure to give my full and unreserved recommendation to Prashob Menon.

headline: Software, High Tech, Semiconductor Productivity- McKinsey & Co.
about:
I guide organizations from good to great. I have a toolkit of strategies, a great record of success, and a great platform for accelerating time-to-market, increasing productivity and decreasing costs. As an expert consultant for 20+ years (McKinsey, Numetrics), I've boosted clients at all levels; I've been called a "CEO whisperer", yet I also have deep practical experience (15 patents) that gives me credibility with CTOs, directors, and line managers. 

At McKinsey, I counseled senior executives of 80+ clients in the areas of software, electronics, product development,  aerospace, telecom, medical, automotive, and consumer. This work increased capacity by 25% and unlocked $600 million in cost savings.

Prior to McKinsey, I co-founded Numetrics Management Systems, a pioneer in machine learning (ML) and big data analytics; used data from more than 10,000 R&D projects to identify two important insights: factors that led to their success and bottlenecks that held them back. Numetrics was acquired by McKinsey in 2013.

My passion for R&D excellence was born from my experience designing leading-edge computing systems. I was head engineer at Supercomputer Systems, a Cray spinoff and startup that held the title of World's Fastest Computer (#1 on the top 500 list). After that, I ran the design enablement organization at Silicon Graphics/SGI, which produced many more of the top 500. I had the privilege of overseeing the integration of hardware design teams after SGI acquired Cray. 

Although it was rewarding to receive those 15 patents based on my technical work, I have found the greatest fulfilment not only in the technical work but in empowering teams as a manager, coach, counselor and motivator. As a board member and senior exec of startups that were both acquired, I've seen the fruits of that labor.  I've also enjoyed sharing perspectives speaking at industry conferences, and I've co-authored two textbooks and numerous research articles.

headline: Associate at McKinsey & Company | Kellogg MBA | Dams Expert | Perpetual Learner
about:
Let’s talk dirty. From river mud to sand on a beach, “dirt” is the colloquial name for the earth beneath our feet. As a dam expert and civil engineering consultant, it’s my responsibility to design infrastructure that doesn’t move, but this would be impossible without first understanding the behavior of the earth our infrastructure is built on. “Dirt” is the foundation of my expertise.

From complex analysis of seismic activity and dam failure mechanisms to creative solutions for construction sequencing, I have worked on a variety of large and challenging high-risk critical infrastructure projects. With a Kellogg MBA, my broadened skillset allows me to connect the dots between seemingly disparate topics to create value and elevate the work of my teams.

When I’m not working, you can find me enjoying the great outdoors or feeding my competitive spirit by playing board games.

education.degree: The Lively City: Behavioral Studies and Public Space Design
education.description: Liveability, lively cities, public life and other concepts describing inviting, vibrant and stimulating urban environments are frequently communicated in new visions for the future of cities today. This focus on ‘urban life’ is a direct reaction to the urban realities created in the 20th Century, where increases in our standards of living and the associated city building processes have created areas in which large and increasing numbers of people have become isolated from each other, socially and geographically. Despite our new awareness for the need to plan for a shared and intensified urban life in sustainable cities, we continue to have difficulties in understanding exactly what this ‘urban life’ is, how much of it we truly want and need, and how we can reconcile the often conflicting and simultaneous needs of people for privacy and social stimulation.

honorsAndAwards.issuedBy: The GW Center for Student Engagement
honorsAndAwards.description:
Awarded to student organization officers who have made a meaningful and lasting impact on their organization and have a demonstrated affinity for the GW community.

Student organizations depend on their officers to help define the missions of their groups, build plans to achieve their goals, and provide encouragement and motivation to members while also managing expectations and providing important oversight. From presidents and treasurers, to vice-presidents and membership chairs, all officers can have an incredible impact on their organization. In 2016, The George Washington University will recognize these individuals for the first time with the Student Organization Officer of the Year Award. Nominations can be for current or immediate past (term ended during this academic year) officers from any student organization registered with the Center for Student Engagement.  Nominees should be officers who have served in their role starting no earlier than January 2018 and no later than November 2018. Nominations should clearly outline how the officer being nominated had a direct impact on their student organization that is meaningful and lasting. Nominees should also have a strong affinity to their organization and the George Washington University in general. Finally, nominees should have proven leadership skills and qualities.  Candidates may be self-nominated or nominated by a peer, faculty or staff member.

publications.title: Side-Chain Engineering in Hydrophilic n-Type π-Conjugated Polymers for Enhanced Reactivity
publications.description: Minor changes to side chains in conjugated polymers (CPs) can have pronounced effects on polymer properties by altering backbone planarity, solubility, and interaction with ions. Here, we report the photocontrolled synthesis of hydrophilic CPs from Grignard monomers and find that switching from alkyl to oligo(ethylene glycol) (OEG) side chains changes their photoreactivity. Specifically, installing hydrophilic side chains on the same monomer core yields higher molecular weight polymers and allows polymerization to proceed with lower-energy red light. Additionally, we discover a side chain decomposition pathway for N-OEG monomers, which are prevalent in CP research. Decomposition can be overcome by adding an extra methylene unit in the side chains without compromising polymer molecular weight or hydrophilicity. Importantly, this polymerization does not require transition metal catalysts and is a promising approach to the preparation of n-type conjugated block copolymers.

publications.title: Light Directs Monomer Coordination in Catalyst-Free Grignard Photopolymerization
publications.description:
Overview: This was one of the mechanisms we never thought we would understand! After some thoughtful experimental design in our lab, finding skilled collaborators, and some great computational growth by Eliot, we were able to understand how our photopolymerization works.
Abstract: π-Conjugated polymers can serve as active layers in flexible and lightweight electronics and are conventionally synthesized by transition-metal-mediated polycondensation at elevated temperatures. We recently reported a photopolymerization of electron-deficient heteroaryl Grignard monomers that enables the catalyst-free synthesis of n-type π-conjugated polymers. Herein, we describe an experimental and computational investigation into the mechanism of this photopolymerization. Spectroscopic studies performed in situ and after quenching reveal that the propagating chain is a radical anion with halide end groups. DFT calculations for model oligomers suggest a Mg-templated SRN1-type coupling, in which Grignard monomer coordination to the radical anion chain avoids the formation of free sp2 radicals and allows C–C bond formation with very low barriers. We find that light plays an unusual role in the reaction, photoexciting the radical anion chain to shift electron density to the termini and thus enabling productive monomer binding.

publications.title: Advances in the Synthesis of π‐Conjugated Polymers by Photopolymerization
publications.description: π‐Conjugated polymers (CPs) combine the flexibility, processability, and lightness of plastics with semiconducting properties for optoelectronic applications. These polymers are conventionally synthesized by thermal transition‐metal‐catalyzed polycondensation. Photochemical approaches to CPs offer the possibility of direct photopatterning, but present mechanistic challenges. Shimidzu first described the photopolymerization of thiophene derivatives in the 1990s, but the field lay dormant for many years. Recently, both oxidative and reductive photopolymerizations have been developed to access p‐type and n‐type materials. This Minireview summarizes these developments and the outlook for this nascent field.

publications.title: Photocontrolled Synthesis of N-Type Conjugated Polymers
publications.description: Current approaches to synthesize π‐conjugated polymers (CPs) are dominated by thermally driven, transition metal‐mediated reactions. Herein we show that electron‐deficient Grignard monomers readily polymerize under visible light irradiation at room temperature in the absence of a catalyst. The product distribution can be tuned by the wavelength of irradiation based on the absorption of the polymer. Conversion studies are consistent with an uncontrolled chain‐growth process; correspondingly, chain extension produces all‐conjugated n‐type block copolymers. Preliminary results demonstrate that the polymerization can be expanded to donor‐acceptor alternating copolymers. We anticipate that this method can serve as a platform to access new architectures of n‐type CPs without the need for transition metal catalysis.
